info.name: RetroFlow QA - Core Business Rules
info.description: API checks for RetroFlow team creation, retrospective lifecycle, feedback immutability, action-item completion, and one explicitly manual concurrency scenario. Run in order. The concurrency folder must be executed by sending its two create requests concurrently from separate tabs; Collection Runner sends requests sequentially and is not valid concurrency evidence. This collection creates persistent QA data and does not clean it up.

exec: pm.test('Concurrent create has no server error', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.below(500); });
pm.test('Request is rejected with a 4xx response', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(400, 499); });
pm.test('Request does not cause a server error', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.below(500); });
pm.test('Request succeeds with a 2xx response', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 299); });
let body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
if (body && name.includes('ACTION setup - Create dedicated open retrospective')) pm.collectionVariables.set('actionRetroId', body.id);
if (body && name.includes('ACTION-01 Create action item')) pm.collectionVariables.set('actionItemId', body.id);
if (body && name.includes('RETRO-05 Create fresh concurrency team')) pm.collectionVariables.set('concurrencyTeamId', body.id);

exec: const items = Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : (payload.retrospectives || payload.content || payload.data);
